notable_teammates.notes: Escoffier offers a massive 55% Cryo and Hydro RES Shred, heals to keep the team alive and stack Furina’s Fanfare, and deals good personal damage.

Vodyanitsa performs on par with Escoffier. She provides Cryo and Hydro RES Shred and two separate sets of Additive Base DMG Bonus scaling with her Max HP, boosting the damage of Skirk and off-field characters.
Furina provides plenty of DMG Bonus, can hold 4pc TotM to further buff Skirk, and deals off-field damage. In teams with Vodyanitsa, Furina ends up holding 4pc Scroll or 4pc Golden Troupe.

Yelan deals high off-field damage and offers a ramping DMG Bonus for the on-field character. She also enables Hydro Resonance to benefit both herself and any other HP-scaling Hydro unit, such as Furina or Vodyanitsa.
Xingqiu serves as a cheaper Hydro alternative to Yelan. He offers off-field damage, interruption resistance, and damage mitigation, but lacks direct ways to buff Skirk’s damage.
Columbina is a subpar option due to her lack of relevant buffs and high opportunity cost on Skirk’s team (i.e. she performs better in Lunar-oriented teams).
Before C6, Candace does not provide off-field Hydro application and cannot help Skirk generate Void Rifts while off-field.
Aino is a free Hydro option obtainable by completing Act I of Nod-Krai’s Archon Quest.

Citlali acts as a Cryo buffer and shielder. She grants the full Cryo DMG% buff from 4pc Scroll, can hold TTDS (at the cost of lower shield HP) or Wandering Evenstar, and enables Eshu for Skirk with her shield.

Shenhe is a powerful Cryo buffer. She offers her Icy Quill buff, Cryo DMG Bonus and RES Shred, and, depending on whether she uses her Tap or Hold Skill, Burst and Skill DMG Bonus or Normal and Charged Attack DMG Bonus.

Mona is a Hydro Catalyst user who can hold TTDS and provide other buffs. Mona grants up to 60% DMG Bonus through her Burst’s Omen debuff, which can be extended through Freeze to cover more of Skirk’s damage window.
Mualani acts as a buffer and battery in Skirk’s teams. She provides the full Cryo and Hydro DMG% buff of 4pc Scroll and holds TTDS. She can easily trigger 4pc Scroll against unfreezable enemies.
Dahlia’s shield enables Eshu for Skirk and provides some additional comfort even with Skirk’s high interruption resistance.
Charlotte provides Cryo application and strong teamwide healing that quickly stacks Furina’s Fanfare. However, she has very high ER requirements while holding TTDS.

Layla’s main benefits come from her shield, which enables Eshu’s passive and provides further interruption resistance. She also provides Cryo application and a modest Normal and Charged Attack buff from her C4.
Rosaria provides a solid CRIT Rate buff as well as some personal damage. The consistent off-field Cryo application from her Elemental Burst can also help maintain uptime on Cryo Resonance.
Mika offers healing to stack Furina’s Fanfare and an Attack SPD buff to let Skirk squeeze in more Normal Attacks.
Chongyun provides a small amount of Attack SPD and Cryo RES Shred, the latter being rare in Freeze teams with limited rosters.
Kokomi can hold TTDS to buff Skirk and heal, but she faces some issues to consider. She only heals the active character, which makes her worse at stacking Furina’s Fanfare than Charlotte.
Barbara can also hold TTDS to buff Skirk, but she has many issues that make her much worse than Charlotte.
Sigewinne offers teamwide healing to stack Fanfare and provides Additive Base DMG Bonus for off-field Skill damage, buffing Furina’s and Escoffier’s damage.
Sigewinne offers teamwide healing to stack Fanfare and provides Additive Base DMG Bonus for off-field Skill damage, buffing Furina’s and Escoffier’s damage.
Diona offers both healing and shielding. However, her healing is limited to the active character, and both her healing output and shield HP are relatively lower than dedicated healers and shielders.
Kaeya is a cheap option for players with limited rosters. Aside from his somewhat low personal damage, Kaeya offers no utility beyond Cryo application and particle generation.
Neuvillette’s high personal damage, flexible rotations, and strong synergy with Skirk’s best teammates make him an excellent pick for Skirk’s quickswap teams.
Ayaka is another strong dual-carry option thanks to her high personal damage.

Similar to Ayaka, Ganyu has the flexibility to swap in and out freely to deal damage while accommodating Skirk’s field-time requirements. Her Burst’s Cryo DMG Bonus also benefits both herself and Skirk.

Other on-field Hydro DPS options for Skirk’s quickswap teams. Though weaker than the above alternatives for Skirk, they still offer fun gameplay and the damage is solid compared to their own other teams.
